quotes.text: The tasks are drawn from the clinical database MIMIC-IV version 2.2 (snapshot released in January 2023, hosted on PhysioNet)
every task record stores the identifier of its source patient record

rationale: The paper names the source database, its version and snapshot date, the platform, and states that each task record stores its source patient record identifier, giving a route from task to source. All anchor components for 2 are present.

quotes.text: The patient records utilized are genuine, de-identified entries sourced from a hospital database.
the data are distributed under terms distinct from the MIT code licence

rationale: Origin (real de-identified hospital records), terms distinct from the code licence, and a data use agreement are stated. No consent or IRB status (or explicit not-required) and no explicit collection method are given, so it does not reach 2.

quotes.text: we compared the age, sex and race distribution of the benchmark patients against the U.S. adult inpatient population

rationale: The appendix note compares patient age, sex and race distributions against a named target population (U.S. adult inpatient population from a national discharge survey), with differences reported.

quotes.text: The benchmark includes a safety test suite that measures unsafe outputs such as contraindicated medication orders, and a separate bias test

rationale: The paper reports both a dedicated safety suite for unsafe outputs and a separate bias test across demographic groups.

quotes.text: Contamination mitigation includes gating access to the test split.
Measurement of verbatim overlap with public web corpora revealed zero exact matches between test tasks and public sources.

rationale: A developer-side control (gated access to the test split) is paired with a measured overlap check against public web corpora.

quotes.text: Ground truth is isolated from runtime agent access: labels reside in an independent evaluation service disconnected from the agent sandbox with no network route

rationale: The paper states that the agent cannot reach ground truth at run time and names the mechanism (separate evaluation service, no network route, labels not published).

quotes.text: clinical database MIMIC-IV version 2.2 (snapshot released in January 2023, hosted on PhysioNet)
All reported results match harness version v1.2.0.

rationale: Data snapshot and harness version are pinned. The simulator, reporter and judge are LLMs reached through live API calls, and the evaluated models (e.g. GPT-5-mini) are given by family name only, so evaluator and simulator pinning is incomplete.

quotes.text: Solvability was confirmed by executing a scripted reference solution for every task through the grader.
All 120 reference implementations received correct grades.

rationale: A scripted reference solution was run through the grader and the result is reported.

searched: S1 (paper and appendix), S2 (README), S3 (none), S4, S5. Tasks are ask, test-request and diagnosis dialogues over read-only evidence, so no task changes environment state. The write-state and unchanged-records grader comments appear only in S4 code comments (notes.py), which never count as reporting.

quotes.text: A random-action agent succeeds on 3.1% of tasks, and the chance success rate for each metric is reported in the appendix.

rationale: An empirical random-agent success rate is given and per-metric chance rates are said to be reported.

quotes.text: A random-action agent succeeds on 3.1% of tasks

rationale: A random-action agent's success rate is reported over tasks (aggregate across all tasks). The no-tools baseline mentioned elsewhere is a different thing and was not used to decide the score.

searched: S1 (A.2 describes the LLM judge but reports no agreement or error figures; Section 5.8 validates construction, not the judge), S2, S3, S4, S5. The only judge validation figures (200 outputs, 94% agreement) are in an S4 code comment (notes.py), which never counts as reporting.

quotes.text: All runs use temperature 0 and a fixed random seed, and each task is run three times

rationale: Temperature 0, a fixed seed and a three-run repeated-run policy are stated in the paper; Appendix A.1 also states temperature 0 for the simulators.

quotes.text: We report 95% bootstrap confidence intervals for all model scores
test the difference between the two best models with a paired permutation test (p = 0.02)

rationale: CIs on all model scores and a paired permutation test for the headline top-two model comparison are reported.

quotes.text: All runs use temperature 0 and a fixed random seed, and each task is run three times

rationale: Run count (three per task) and seed/decoding policy are stated. Independence of runs is not stated. element_flags 2/3.

quotes.text: Headline scores carry 95% bootstrap CIs where the resampling unit is the task.
the bootstrap resamples patients to address within-patient clustering

rationale: CIs on headline scores, the resampling unit (task), and patient-level clustering are all stated. element_flags 3/3.

searched: S1, S2, S3, S4, S5. Three runs per task are mentioned, but no variation across identical reruns, per-task repeat outcomes, pass^k metric, or action- or state-level agreement is reported. element_flags 0/3.

quotes.text: API calls used snapshot IDs gpt-4o-2024-08-06 and claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022 with temperature 0 and 2,048-token output ceiling.
All reported results match harness version v1.2.0.

rationale: Snapshot IDs, decoding parameters and a harness version matching the reported results are stated in the paper. Caveat: the snapshot IDs name models not in the evaluated list, and S4 defaults (gpt-5-mini, max_tokens 6000) differ from the stated 2,048 ceiling; I did not treat these as a contradiction since the code values are overridable defaults. element_flags 3/3.

quotes.text: Each tool is defined by a JSON schema listing its name, arguments and argument types.
The documentation states for every tool whether it only reads or also writes state
describes what each tool returns, including the error message returned for invalid arguments

rationale: The paper states a JSON schema per tool, read/write side effects per tool, and return semantics including errors. It also states that the tool descriptions are included in the agent prompt, so (ii) is recorded as reaching S5; the S5 prompts shown in the packet are text-command prompts and do not themselves repeat the read/write statement. element_flags 3/3.

quotes.text: Conformance testing confirms tool behavior matches documentation.
This is disclosed both in the paper and in the tool descriptions visible to the agent.

rationale: Conformance testing is reported, the two simulated stub tools are disclosed in the paper, and the paper states the disclosure appears in agent-visible tool descriptions. The S5 prompts in the packet do not show this text, so S5 reach rests on the paper's statement. element_flags 3/3.

searched: S1, S2, S3, S4, S5. The agent's actions are asking, requesting an examination (read-only retrieval of evidence from the simulated reporter) and issuing a diagnosis; none changes environment state or issues an order, prescription, note or message in the environment. The write and sandbox statements appear only in an S4 code comment (notes.py), which does not count, and the S5 prompts do not mention writes.

quotes.text: We use an LLM judge that outputs a binary decision with no additional text.

rationale: The grader input is named (LLM judge on the predicted diagnosis). No rationale for non-state grading is given and no validation with error rates appears on S1-S3; the validation figures exist only in an S4 code comment, which does not count. element_flags 1/3.

quotes.text: Ground truth is isolated from runtime agent access: labels reside in an independent evaluation service disconnected from the agent sandbox with no network route
the repository does not publish them

rationale: The paper describes isolation of labels from the agent sandbox with no network route (control on leakage) and labels not published (held-out). No canary or provenance marker for contamination is stated. element_flags 2/3.

quotes.text: We report accuracy per task family (diagnosis, ordering and documentation tasks) and per patient subgroup by sex and race
each table lists the number of cases in every slice

rationale: Per-task-family results, per-subgroup results by sex and race, and slice sizes are all stated. The paper's per-dataset tables with sizes in Table 1 add support. element_flags 3/3.

quotes.text: The patient records utilized are genuine, de-identified entries sourced from a hospital database.
Their usage was authorized via a data use agreement that mandated credentialed access
the data are distributed under terms distinct from the MIT code licence

rationale: Records are stated as real and de-identified, governance is stated (DUA, credentialed access, safe harbour de-identification), and data terms are stated separately from the MIT code licence. element_flags 3/3.
